intro: A masked image encoder processes only visible patches. A decoder needs the original sequence order with placeholders in the missing positions.
task: Scatter visible patch embeddings into their original positions and fill all other positions with a mask token.
requirements: visible is a nonempty patches-by-features matrix. positions is a same-length vector of distinct integer indices in 0..total-1; total is an integer 1..64. mask_token is a feature vector of matching width.
Return {"tokens": total-by-features matrix, "masked": boolean vector}. masked is True exactly where no visible embedding was supplied. Visible positions may be unsorted.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Initialize every row with the mask token, then scatter the supplied rows.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Sorting positions without applying the same permutation to visible would mismatch patches.

explanation: Restoring order makes the decoder’s positional layout match the original image grid. The visible rows arrive in encoder order, so the position mapping must be applied to each corresponding embedding.
A mask token is an embedding rather than a literal zero. Returning the mask separately keeps missingness observable even when a visible embedding happens to equal the token.
